prompt:
A black-and-white CHILDREN'S COLORING BOOK page, square 1:1, 1080x1080. Composition must be SQUARE, never wide or landscape.

CRITICAL — READ FIRST: (a) the drawing must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES with NO frame, NO border line, NO box and NO white margin band; (b) the Borrelia must be a deeply coiled CORKSCREW SPIRAL of at least four full S-curves, not a smooth blob.

SCENE: A friendly cartoon BORRELIA character — a long, wiggly, corkscrew-shaped noodle bacterium — is peeking cheerfully out of the back of a big cartoon TICK that is clinging to a tall blade of grass, while an enormous friendly pair of TWEEZERS reaches in from the side to lift the tick off. Playful and reassuring, never scary.
- The BORRELIA is a LONG SPRING-SHAPED CORKSCREW: its body must wind through AT LEAST FOUR full deep S-curves, like a stretched-out bedspring, a curly telephone cord or a twisted ribbon of pasta. This spiral is the single most important feature of the whole picture — a straight, smooth, blobby or single-bend body is WRONG and the page is rejected. The curves are big, loose and open, with clear white space inside every bend. It has a BIG FRIENDLY FACE at its front end: two large round eyes with pupils, cheerful curved eyebrows and a wide happy open grin, plus two tiny stubby waving arms. Its body loops out of a little round hatch on the tick's back and curls across the scene in big open wavy loops with plenty of white space inside each curve.
- The TICK is a chunky, rounded, good-natured cartoon bug, roughly the size of a large plum in the picture, drawn from the side. It has a small oval head, a big smooth teardrop-shaped body divided into a few large simple plates, eight short stubby legs with rounded feet, and its own simple friendly face with two dot eyes and a small wobbly smile. It is holding on to the grass blade with its front legs.
- The BLADE OF GRASS is a broad, tall, gently curving strap-shaped leaf that the tick sits on, with a simple centre vein line, rising from the bottom of the picture. Two or three more big simple grass blades and one round chunky clover leaf grow around it and run off the bottom and side edges.
- The TWEEZERS are huge, chunky and friendly: two long tapering arms joined at a rounded hinge, coming in from the upper side of the picture, their blunt rounded tips opening around the tick right down at the grass where it grips. Give the tweezers a cheerful little face near the hinge — two round eyes and a small smile — so they read as a helpful friend arriving, not a threat.
- Everything is drawn LARGE, SIMPLE and CHUNKY, with generous open white areas inside every shape so a child can colour them in.

STYLE — coloring book line art:
- BOLD, THICK, EVEN BLACK OUTLINES on pure WHITE. Every shape fully closed.
- ABSOLUTELY NO shading, NO grey tones, NO hatching, NO stippling, NO cross-hatching, NO gradients, NO colour fill, NO solid black areas anywhere (eyes may have a small solid pupil only).
- Simple, cheerful, chunky cartoon shapes with plenty of white space.

STRICTLY FORBIDDEN — the page is rejected if any of these appear:
- ANY decorative STARBURST, comic-style radiating burst, "pow"/impact star, sparkle burst, twinkle burst, sunbeam rays, radiating speed lines, motion rays or halo of rays behind, around or under any character. NO radiating lines of any kind anywhere. They leave a big empty shape that cannot be removed afterwards.
- ANY rectangle, rounded rectangle, square box outline, picture frame, panel edge, comic panel, border line, outer margin line, ground-line box, or vignette. The drawing must NOT sit inside a box of any kind. Do NOT draw a thin black line anywhere near the edge of the image. There must be NO white margin between the artwork and the image edge — leaves and grass are CUT OFF by the image edge itself.
- The artwork must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES of the square — the grass blades, leaves and background elements run right off the top, bottom, left and right edges, with no white margin band and no enclosing outline.
- NO text, letters, numbers, words, captions, labels, signatures or watermarks anywhere.
- NO speech bubble, thought bubble or balloon of any kind (one is added separately afterwards).
- NO blood, no bite wound, no red marks, no frightened or angry faces, nothing gruesome.
- NO human figure, no hand holding the tweezers — the tweezers float in on their own as a friendly character.
